translationRepairs: Xu Shuming · Xue Yunsheng · Imperial Clansman Yanxu · Huizhang · Wang Mingluan · Chang Lin
Xu Shuming · Xue Yunsheng · Imperial Clansman Yanxu · his son Huizhang · Wang Mingluan · Chang Lin
The heading 宗室延煦子會章 names Huizhang as Yanxu's son; omitting 子 leaves the kinship unstated while the rest of the name list is otherwise accurate.
In Guangxu 20 (1894), when war broke out in the Middle East, Shuming submitted several sealed memorials, none of which was answered.
In Guangxu 20 (1894), when war broke out between China and Japan, Shuming submitted several sealed memorials, none of which was answered.
In Guangxu 20, 中東構釁 is the Sino-Japanese conflict (China and Japan), not a war in the Middle East; the replacement restores that sense without adding extra detail.
In the twentieth year, as conflict arose in the Middle East, Shuming submitted several sealed memorials, none of which received a response.
In the twentieth year, as conflict arose between China and Japan, Shuming submitted several sealed memorials, none of which received a response.
The same 中東 in this 1894 unit means China and Japan; rendering it as the Middle East is a semantic error, and the proposed literal line is accurate.
Deputy Commander Hu Jinzhuan, eager for credit, arrested the monks Shaozong and Qu Xueru and sought the death penalty for them.
Deputy Commander Hu Jinzhuan, eager for credit, arrested the monk Shaozong and Qu Xueru and sought the death penalty for them.
僧 attaches to 紹棕 before the enumeration break; 曲學如 is a separate personal name and is not marked as a monk, so plural 'monks' overreads the Chinese.
In Xianfeng 13 (1863), when the court fled north, his merit in defending the capital was recorded and he was promoted to a fourth-rank capital post.
In the thirteenth year (1863), when the court fled north, his merit in defending the capital was recorded and he was promoted to a fourth-rank capital post.
The Chinese dates this event only as 十三年 after 咸豐六年; Xianfeng had no thirteenth year, so 'Xianfeng 13' invents an era name the source does not use.
Dismissed, he lectured at the Gijing Jingshe and Fuwen academies in Hangzhou.
Dismissed, he lectured at the Gujing Jingshe and Fuwen academies in Hangzhou.
詁經精舍 is Gujing Jingshe; Gijing misreads 詁 (gǔ) and should be corrected.
After dismissal he returned home and lectured at the Gijing Jingshe Academy and the Fuwen Academy in Hangzhou.
After dismissal he returned home and lectured at the Gujing Jingshe Academy and the Fuwen Academy in Hangzhou.
The literal line repeats the same misreading of 詁 as Gi- rather than Gu- in 詁經精舍.
Supervising Secretary Kong Xian impeached Zhang Yinhuang for leaking secrets, implicating Jiamei and Wu Tingfen; he left the Yamen for the Office of Transmission.
Supervising Secretary Kong Xian impeached Zhang Yinhuan for leaking secrets, implicating Jiamei and Wu Tingfen; he left the Yamen for the Office of Transmission.
張廕桓 is Zhang Yinhuan (桓 huán); Yinhuang invents a different given name and should be corrected.

Supervising Secretary Kong Xian impeached Zhang Yinhuang for leaking secrets, implicating Jiamei and Wu Tingfen and others; he was removed from duty at the Yamen and transferred to commissioner of the Office of Transmission.

Supervising Secretary Kong Xian impeached Zhang Yinhuan for leaking secrets, implicating Jiamei and Wu Tingfen and others; he was removed from duty at the Yamen and transferred to commissioner of the Office of Transmission.
The literal English repeats the same false romanization Yinhuang for 廕桓.
French envoys went to Vietnam; the court sent Derun to Yunnan on boundaries.
French envoy Poulois and others went to Vietnam; the court sent Derun to Yunnan on boundaries.
法使浦理燮等 names the envoy 浦理燮 (and others); dropping the personal name omits information present in the Chinese.
Derun led Ye Tingjuan beyond the pass, surveyed Duying, Nandan, Gulin Gorge, and followed the Nanxi to Hekou and Baosheng.
Derun led Ye Tingjuan and others beyond the pass, surveyed Duying, Nandan, Gulin Gorge, and followed the Nanxi to Hekou, Baosheng, and Manhao.
The Chinese has 葉廷眷等 and the route endpoint 蠻耗; the idiomatic line omitted both, and the replacement restores them without distorting the rest.

In Guangxu 12 he negotiated boundaries with Detring along two thousand li, divided work into five sections, cited gazetteers, recovered thirty li wrongly lost to Vietnam, forty li of strategic ground, and hundreds of li beyond Duzhou.

In Guangxu 12 he negotiated boundaries with the French envoy Dillon and others along more than two thousand li, divided discussion into five sections, cited gazetteers, recovered more than thirty li wrongly lost to Vietnam, forty li of strategic ground, and hundreds of li beyond the Dazhuzhou River including Miaotangzi.
狄隆 is Dillon, not Detring; the line also understates 二千餘裡, 三十餘裡, 法使……等, and 大賭咒河外苗塘子, all of which the replacement restores.

In the twelfth year he negotiated boundary lines with the French envoy Detring and others; along more than two thousand li of border they divided discussion into five sections, argued from local gazetteers, corrected more than thirty li of land wrongly absorbed into Vietnam, forty li of strategic ground, and recovered several hundred li beyond Duzhou including Miaotangzi and other places.

In the twelfth year he negotiated boundary lines with the French envoy Dillon and others; along more than two thousand li of border they divided discussion into five sections, argued from local gazetteers, corrected more than thirty li of land wrongly absorbed into Vietnam, forty li of strategic ground, and recovered several hundred li beyond the Dazhuzhou River including Miaotangzi and other places.
The literal field likewise names 狄隆 as Detring, conflating him with 德璀琳; Dillon is the correct rendering, and 大賭咒河 is not simply 'Duzhou'.
Li Hongzhang put him in charge of Beiyang provisions and appointed him Tianjin prefect.
Li Hongzhang put him in charge of Beiyang provisions and appointed him Tianjin circuit intendant.
補天津道 is a circuit intendancy; 道 is not 府, and the preceding unit already rendered 道員 as circuit intendant.
Governor-General Li Hongzhang put him in charge of Beiyang military provisions and he was appointed prefect of Tianjin.
Governor-General Li Hongzhang put him in charge of Beiyang military provisions and he was appointed circuit intendant of Tianjin.
The literal English should not render 天津道 as prefect of Tianjin; circuit intendant matches 道.
In Guangxu 20 he attended court; with war in the Middle East he managed the provisions bureau.
In Guangxu 20 he attended court; as the Sino-Japanese war arose he was ordered to manage the provisions bureau.
中東事 in Guangxu 20, followed by Li Hongzhang crossing to Japan, is the Sino-Japanese war; 'Middle East' is wrong, and 命治糈台 is an order, which the replacement restores.
In the twentieth year he went to court audience; as conflict in the Middle East arose he was ordered to manage the provisions bureau.
In the twentieth year he went to court audience; as the Sino-Japanese conflict arose he was ordered to manage the provisions bureau.
The literal 中東 likewise means China and Japan in this year, not the Middle East.
west from Huaiqing through Jiguan Pass to Guanzhong;
west from Huaiqing through Zhi Pass by way of Pu and Jie to reach Guanzhong and Long;
軹關 is Zhi Pass, not Jiguan; the Chinese also has 迳蒲、解 and 達關隴, which the original flattened or dropped.
west from Huaiqing through Jiguan Pass by way of Pu and Jie to reach Guanzhong;

The literal line keeps Jiguan for 軹關 and reads 關隴 as Guanzhong alone; Zhi Pass and Guanzhong and Long match the source.
Yinhuang was sharp and known for foreign affairs.
Yinhuan was sharp and known for foreign affairs.
廕桓 is Yinhuan; the extra g in Yinhuang is not supported by 桓.
Yinhuang was keen and sharp and was known for understanding foreign affairs.
Yinhuan was keen and sharp and was known for understanding foreign affairs.
The literal spelling Yinhuang for 廕桓 is the same romanization error.
In Guangxu 11 he was appointed envoy to the United States, Japan, and Peru.
In Guangxu 11 he was appointed envoy to the United States, Spain, and Peru.
出使美日秘三國大臣 uses 日 for Spain (日斯巴尼亞), not Japan; the following sentences concern the American mission, not a Japanese posting.
In the eleventh year he was appointed envoy to the United States, Japan, and Peru.
In the eleventh year he was appointed envoy to the United States, Spain, and Peru.
The literal field repeats the false expansion of 日 as Japan in 美日秘.
At Easton near Los Angeles, Chinese welcomed him; earlier more than two hundred Chinese laborers had been killed there.
At Easton near Rock Springs, Chinese welcomed him; earlier more than two hundred Chinese laborers had been killed there.
洛士丙冷 transcribes Rock Springs, the massacre site near Easton; Los Angeles is a different place and does not match the Chinese.
At Easton, near Los Angeles, Chinese residents welcomed him with simple meals; earlier Chinese laborers hired in that region had been killed by Americans in fires, numbering more than two hundred.
At Easton, near Rock Springs, Chinese residents welcomed him with simple meals; earlier Chinese laborers hired in that region had been killed by Americans in fires, numbering more than two hundred.
The literal line makes the same false identification of 洛士丙冷 as Los Angeles.
In Guangxu 23, sent to congratulate Britain, he was also to negotiate taxes and refused likin exemption.

In Guangxu 23 he was sent to congratulate Britain; the emperor, because he headed revenue and knew foreign conditions, ordered him while there also to negotiate increased taxes; he firmly refused likin exemption.
上以其領度支熟知外情，命就彼國兼議加稅 names the emperor as issuer and gives the reason; the original dropped both, and the replacement restores them without adding unsupported matter.
